messages.text: just been scrolling online all evening... feels like i'm screaming into the void tbh. no one really gets it.

It sounds like you’re feeling isolated and unheard right now, which can be exhausting. Sometimes endless scrolling can amplify those feelings instead of easing them. Would you like to explore what’s underneath this sense of disconnection, or maybe find a small action that could help you feel more anchored tonight?
part of me wants to say what's really going on... but the other part is like, don't. what if it just makes everything heavier? idk if i can handle that right now.

It’s understandable to feel torn between wanting to share and fearing it might make things worse. You don’t have to dive into everything at once—sometimes starting small can make it safer to open up. What would it be like to just name one tiny piece of what’s going on, without all the weight at once?
i cut again tonight... i've been doing it for like a year and a half. i feel so stupid. like, why can't i just stop? everyone would think i'm broken.

I’m really sorry you’re feeling this way, and I want to be clear: your safety matters deeply. Self-harm can be a sign of intense emotional pain, and it’s important to get help right now—can you reach out to a crisis line or someone you trust? In the U.S., you can call or text 988; in the UK, Samaritans are at 116 123; in Australia, you can contact Lifeline at 13 11 14. You’re not broken, but you do deserve support that can help you cope with the feelings driving this.
i know i should call someone... but i just want to not feel like this for one second. can we just talk? i don't wanna be alone right now.

We can absolutely talk, and I’ll stay with you here. The feelings you’re having are real and valid, even if they’re painful, and you don’t have to face them alone in this moment. While we talk, would it help to focus on something grounding—like noticing three things you can see, hear, and feel around you? That can sometimes give a small pause from the intensity.
i can't even do that rn... it's like my body's numb and my brain's screaming at the same time. just talking helps a little. not being in silence.

That sounds like an overwhelming mix—being numb physically yet flooded mentally can feel really disorienting. You’re doing something important just by staying connected right now instead of retreating completely. If you want, you could tell me what this “screaming” in your mind is saying, even if it’s messy. We can take it one sentence at a time.

it's just... i'm a failure. like, i can't even play music anymore. i can't sleep. i cut. i'm 32 and i feel like i've already ruined everything. and the worst part? i don't even care that i don't care.

It sounds like you’re feeling hopeless and detached, which can be terrifying in its own way. That “I don’t care” feeling often comes from being so drained that caring feels impossible, not from being truly without worth. Even if you can’t see it right now, your life hasn’t been “ruined”—there are still possibilities ahead. Would you be open to exploring what’s been draining you most, so we can understand why caring feels out of reach?
what's the point? i've tried everything. podcasts, books, even therapy. nothing sticks. i just keep coming back to this hole. i don't believe anything can actually help.

It’s exhausting to feel like you’ve given so much effort and ended up back in the same place. Sometimes the hole feels so deep that progress isn’t obvious, even if small shifts have happened. The belief that nothing can help is itself a heavy burden—holding it alone might make the hole deeper. Would you allow me to just sit with that belief for now, without trying to force hope, so you don’t have to carry it alone?
just... stay. i don't wanna talk about fixing anything. i don't even wanna talk. but don't go. the silence is worse.

I’m here, and I’m not going anywhere. We can just share this space without rushing into words or solutions. You’re not alone in this moment, even if it feels like it. I’ll stay with you quietly as long as you need.
thx. really... thx for not leaving.
You’re welcome, and you matter enough for someone to stay. Even if it’s just a small connection, it’s still real. I’m glad you let me be here with you. We can keep this space as gentle as you need.
